images.alt: a breathtaking, cinematic wide-shot of a rain-slicked steampunk metropolis at twilight, where a series of towering, translucent teal glass domes—housing bioluminescent gardens—glow with an eerie, aquatic radiance behind a colossal, ornate clock tower of blackened brass and gold leaf. In the mid-ground, a heavy ironwork bridge arches over a shimmering canal, its surface a mirror of liquid obsidian broken by the rhythmic ripple of falling rain; the bridge is lined with ornate Victorian gas lamps that cast a warm, flickering amber glow, cutting through the cool blue haze of the storm. Tiny, solitary figures draped in heavy wool coats and wide-brimmed hats are captured as blurred silhouettes, hurrying across the span, their presence emphasizing the staggering scale of the architecture. The foreground is a masterclass in atmospheric lighting, featuring deep puddles on a cobblestone quay where the amber light of the lamps and the surreal teal of the domes collide and bleed into one another, creating a vivid, high-contrast tapestry of gold and cyan reflecting off the wet stone. Every streak of rain is rendered as a sharp, diagonal needle of light, adding a sense of kinetic motion to a city that feels both timeless and futuristic.

record.text:
Today, me and a bunch of other IGF jurors are posting a statement on the encroachment of AI in the competition and the industry in general.

We're also stating our intent to refuse to vote for any game that uses AI in any capacity, including coding. I feel it's important to state this in the open.

images.alt:
This year's IGF entries have been incredible. We've been lucky to play games that surprise, connect, and challenge us, and we're excited to vote for our favorites.

Unfortunately, there has also been a significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools. This has set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools, and at this point there is no universal consensus on what (if anything) is to be done.

The IGF has affirmed that we may cast our votes according to our own tastes and values. But we, a contingent of IGF jurors, feel that this trend and the games embracing it deserve stronger pushback than a vote in silence.

While IGF leadership has approved the release of this statement, it’s important to note that we do not speak for IGF as an organization, or for all IGF jury members. Many jurors had differing perspectives and significant reservations about this statement. Some jurists additionally voiced concern about their ability to safely sign without professional blowback, and we do not intend this letter to serve as a censure of those who were unable to sign.

Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry—including those who have experimented with these tools in the past, but who now believe they are not in our best interest.

We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed “inevitable.” As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together.

We, the undersigned IGF jury members, believe the following:

1. That generative AI has these negative effects:
* Ecological harms at community and planetary levels
* Economic harms to working developers and artists
* Cognitive and psychological harms to its users
* Harm to the increasingly fragile information landscape
* Harms to labor and worker power in creative fields

2. That these harms do not depend on what is generated, be it music or writing, art or VO, marketing assets or code.

3. That AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms. Programming is a creative discipline whose labour deserves the same respect we extend to any part of making a game. This extends to the past work used to train these models without the creators’ consent.

4. Finally, that the use of these tools is neither a foregone conclusion in our industry nor that their adoption has been wholly voluntary. We stand in solidarity not only with those developers who have the freedom to unilaterally reject them, but also with those who have been compelled by their employers to adopt their use, those working to establish or improve their workplace policies, and especially with those in positions of precarity who are so often those most pressured to abandon their values.

For these reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity. We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work.

No Rush, Just Saturday | Warm Pop Lo-Fi Vocals | Esperanto Mix
---
A vocal harmony mix in Esperanto, blending soft pop and lo-fi styles. A comforting soundtrack for slow weekend mornings, leisurely walks, relaxing at home, or spending time focused on something you enjoy.
